record.title: A staged LLM pipeline reports Lean-checked runtime proofs for designed optimization algorithms
record.summary: An October 26 preprint reports a staged pipeline in which LLMs propose black-box optimization algorithms and construct potential functions and runtime analyses that are checked by Lean. The author reports that 12 of 15 frontier-model runs across eight problem classes completed the pipeline; nine produced polynomial query bounds without relying on uncharged offline computation. The paper reports an O(n²) result for CycleUncover and matching O(n²) order for LeadingOnes. These are preprint-reported results, not independent reproduction. The study did not empirically compare the algorithms, tested open-weight models did not complete the pipeline, the search space is restricted, and the bounds are not yet state of the art.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A version 1 preprint titled 'Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean' was posted to arXiv on October 26, 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The author reports a staged pipeline combining LLM-proposed black-box optimization algorithms with Lean-checked formal stages. Across eight problem classes, 12 of 15 frontier-model runs completed the pipeline; nine obtained polynomial query bounds without relying on offline computation uncharged in the black-box model. The reported outcomes include O(n²) for CycleUncover and matching O(n²) order for LeadingOnes.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independently reproduced results, broad transfer beyond its selected problem classes, state-of-the-art algorithm performance, or empirical superiority over competing algorithms. It reports no empirical algorithm comparisons; tested open-weight models did not complete the pipeline.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or mathematical review of the reported Lean-checked algorithms and runtime claims was found or performed in this review.
The inspected preprint describes Lean checks and gives extensive appendices, but this activation did not inspect the linked code/Lean repository or rerun reported jobs.
The experiments cover selected bitstring black-box problem classes, include uncharged offline computation in the query model, and report no empirical comparison of the resulting algorithms.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently reproduced and extended, an agent pipeline that proposes optimization algorithms and constructs machine-checked runtime bounds could materially expand AI-assisted algorithm discovery. The reported demonstrations are limited to eight black-box problem classes and frontier-model runs; tested open-weight runs did not complete, the bounds are not state of the art, and no empirical algorithm comparisons were made.
limitations: The evidence is one author-reported preprint; no independent reproduction or specialist review was located in this bounded check.
The paper reports no empirical comparison of algorithms; runtime claims are within the specified black-box query model, which does not charge offline computation between queries.
Only frontier models completed the pipeline in the reported study; the tested open-weight models did not complete it.
The search is restricted to bitstring problems and the paper states the bounds are not yet state of the art.

The author reports that 12 of 15 frontier-model runs across eight problem classes completed the pipeline; nine produced polynomial query bounds without relying on uncharged offline computation. The paper reports an O(n²) result for CycleUncover and matching O(n²) order for LeadingOnes. These are preprint-reported results, not independent reproduction. technical.claimed_result: 12 of 15 frontier-model runs completed across eight problem classes; nine gave polynomial query bounds without relying on uncharged offline computation. Reported examples include O(n²) on CycleUncover and LeadingOnes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint and its reported methods/results are publicly accessible. This activation did not run the paper's pipeline, inspect its code or Lean artifacts, or independently verify the proofs or algorithm comparisons.
technical.mechanism: A staged pipeline elicits informal algorithm proposals, formalizes candidate algorithms and potential functions, then asks an LLM to prove drift conditions and runtime bounds in Lean. Lean proof obligations filter designs that fail specified properties.
technical.regime: Eight black-box optimization problem classes, with 15 reported frontier-model runs plus separate open-weight and ablation runs. The runtime model counts oracle queries and does not charge offline computation between queries.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper reports exponential expected runtime for the classical (1+1) EA on its CycleUncover problem and an O(n²) designed algorithm; it reports matching O(n²) order on LeadingOnes. The claims are author-reported formal results and not independent performance comparisons.

brief.title: A staged LLM pipeline reports Lean-checked runtime proofs for designed optimization algorithms
brief.why_it_matters: If independently reproduced and extended, a process that jointly designs algorithms and machine-checks runtime bounds could expand AI-assisted algorithm discovery. The current evidence is a single author-reported preprint with constrained benchmarks and no empirical comparison of algorithm performance.
